- Over four decades of precision engineering experience since incorporation in 1981, with customer relationships spanning generations of technology - 40% of client relationships are 20+ years old and a further 20% are 10+ years old.

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Economic and geopolitical volatility — Inflation, geopolitical uncertainty, trade tensions, tariff changes and external demand volatility may affect customer schedules, exports, input costs and operating continuity; the Company monitors order-book trends and diversifies across sectors, customers and geographies.
- Market and technology transition — Changes in customer preferences, electrification, xEV adoption and regulatory requirements may affect product relevance and programme opportunities; mitigated by expanding the technology-agnostic and xEV portfolio and participation in ADS and semiconductor applications.
- Talent availability and capability — Growth, innovation and execution may be constrained by the availability, retention and development of skilled technical, operational and leadership talent.
- Counterparty and credit exposure — Customer or financial counterparty defaults may affect revenue realisation, cash flows and financial stability.
- Competition and margin pressure — Increased competition in domestic and international markets may pressure market share, pricing power and margins.
- Liquidity and funding flexibility — Insufficient liquidity or constrained funding access may affect the Company's ability to meet obligations and fund growth initiatives.
- Procurement and supply-chain disruption — Supplier instability, input price volatility, logistics disruption and dependency on limited sources may affect production continuity and cost efficiency.
- Cybersecurity and information protection — Cyber intrusion, system vulnerabilities or data breaches may affect data integrity, sensitive information, business continuity and reputation.

outlook.body:
- Strengthen the core automotive franchise while accelerating growth in technology-agnostic, xEV, aerospace, defence and semiconductor applications, so as to build a more diversified, higher-value precision engineering platform.
- Scale the Aerospace, Defence and Semiconductor (ADS) business as the pillar of diversification, prioritising it for strategic capital allocation given its multi-year revenue visibility.
- Expand machining capability horizontally and vertically - 5-axis machining now handles components up to four metres versus around 1.5 metres previously - to access larger, more complex and higher value-added structural, engine and precision contracts.
- Enter cold and warm forging through a 60:40 joint venture with Nichidai Corporation of Japan, expanding into driveline and steering systems and developing components for humanoid robotics and autonomous mobility platforms, reducing dependence on traditional IC engine components.
- Aggressively expand the manufacturing footprint into new geographies - Pantnagar, a new Manesar hub on long-term lease, expanded Pune operations, and a new ADS hangar - to capture regional outsourcing opportunities.
- Pursue a deliberate high-automation strategy targeting an 80% robotics ratio across all new production lines to counter emerging labour shortages while sharpening precision and consistency.
- Deepen deep-technology exposure through an increased stake in MMRFIC, gaining access to radar and space programmes under the Make in India initiative.
- Stand ready to establish a machining facility in the US once tariff stability is confirmed, in order to defend and grow the international order book.
- Remain technology-agnostic across ICE, hybrid and xEV platforms so the portfolio stays relevant through the mobility transition.
- Growth strategy pillars stated by management: fuelling growth through capacity building; leveraging opportunity in emerging auto technologies; amplifying efficiency through digitisation and innovation; bolstering prospects with strategic investment; and future-proofing the business with strategic diversification.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Sansera operates 18 integrated manufacturing facilities, comprising 17 in India and one specialised facility in Sweden, and continued to expand its production network across both automotive and ADS businesses during FY2025-26. The Company commissioned the approximately 2.7 Lacs sq. ft. Pantnagar facility dedicated to crankshaft assemblies for the domestic two-wheeler segment, featuring IoT-enabled automation, and commenced regular production of semiconductor components. It is accelerating ADS expansion through a new 80,000 sq. ft. hangar scheduled to become operational during 2026-27, which will significantly augment aerospace manufacturing capacity, alongside its existing 1,40,000 sq. ft. ADS manufacturing facility with dedicated Aerospace, Semiconductor and Defence capacity supporting execution of the cumulative order backlog over approximately five years. The Board approved the acquisition of 10 acres of land near Bengaluru International Airport as a strategic base for the next phase of ADS growth. A new manufacturing hub was established at Manesar through a long-term lease for passenger vehicle and two-wheeler components, while existing Pune and Pantnagar operations are being expanded, and the Sweden facility continues as a specialised hub for large-engine connecting rods serving marine and heavy-duty commercial vehicle applications. Machining capacity at existing facilities continues to expand, supported by a planned capex of Rs 2,500 mn over the next few years towards buildings, machinery and advanced manufacturing infrastructure. An in-house surface treatment facility is being commissioned to enable production of larger, more complex structural components and deepen vertical integration, and 5-axis machining capability has been extended from components of around 1.5 metres to components up to 4 metres. Future investments will focus on ADS capacity expansion, additional forging capacity at Pantnagar Plant 6, higher machining capacity at Bengaluru Plant 2, and the Nichidai-Sansera joint venture for technology-agnostic and xEV precision components, where a dedicated manufacturing facility is under development with equipment installation planned through 2026-27 and commercial production expected in the second half of 2026-27.

outlook.body:
- Revenue growth supported by core platform demand, new programme ramp-ups and strong momentum in ADS product sales.
- Margin improvement driven by operating leverage, productivity gains, automation, cost discipline, better utilisation and a richer business mix.
- PAT growth enabled by EBITDA expansion, lower finance cost and sharper execution across operating and financial levers.
- Business mix enhanced by rising contribution from non-automotive, technology-agnostic and xEV-linked opportunities.
- At home the automotive industry is experiencing a healthy recovery, with entry-level motorcycle and passenger vehicle segments poised for strong volume expansion in the year ahead, giving a stable domestic base.
- Aerospace order books remain at historic heights, reflecting sustained global demand, while the semiconductor industry is in a transformative upcycle driven by the worldwide race to build AI infrastructure.
- Stricter Regional Value Content requirements and a decisive shift towards localised manufacturing in North America are reshaping global supply chains and redrawing where value must be created.
- Demand is shifting towards larger, more complex and higher value-added components, aligning with Sansera's expanded machining capability.
- OEMs and global customers are prioritising dependable suppliers with manufacturing depth and quality systems, enhancing Sansera's relevance as a supply-chain-resilience and localisation beneficiary.
- Aerospace components require stringent quality standards, extended qualification cycles, traceability and material discipline, creating strong entry barriers that favour incumbent qualified suppliers.
- Semiconductor equipment components demand exacting dimensional accuracy, surface finish, cleanliness and material integrity, with long qualification cycles favouring trusted suppliers.
- Order inflows from international customers remained subdued during the year due to global macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty.
- India's automotive industry outlook is supported by improving consumer sentiment, better financing availability and resilient demand across two-wheelers, passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles and three-wheelers, sustaining demand for precision-engineered components.
- EV transition and hybrid adoption create opportunities in xEV and technology-agnostic products while supporting portfolio diversification.
- Key watch areas flagged by management: commodity prices, geopolitical uncertainty, logistics disruption, currency volatility and evolving policy frameworks, requiring continued cost discipline and supply-chain resilience.
- The secured order book stood at approximately Rs 19,194 million as of March 2026, representing the peak annual revenue potential of confirmed programmes including letters of intent and purchase orders where production has commenced after 1 April 2026 or is yet to begin.
- The order book is expected to reach peak annual revenue contribution over the next three years as programmes mature and production ramps up.
- The ADS business had a cumulative unexecuted order backlog of approximately Rs 44,638 million (Rs 44.6 bn) as of 31 March 2026, expected to be executed over the next five years, providing an unusual degree of multi-year revenue visibility.
- The order book as of 31 March 2026 includes programmes that entered mass production on or after 1 April 2026, whose full revenue potential is expected to be reflected progressively in the topline as they reach peak production levels.
- Order inflows from international customers remained subdued during the year due to prevailing global macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties, though the Company continues to actively pursue new orders across all business segments.
- The Value Creation Model cites a strong order book of Rs 19.2 bn as an input for the year.

currentContext.expansion: Sansera operates 18 integrated manufacturing facilities, comprising 17 in India and one specialised facility in Sweden, and continued to expand its production network across both automotive and ADS businesses during FY2025-26. The Company commissioned the approximately 2.7 Lacs sq. ft. Pantnagar facility dedicated to crankshaft assemblies for the domestic two-wheeler segment, featuring IoT-enabled automation, and commenced regular production of semiconductor components. It is accelerating ADS expansion through a new 80,000 sq. ft. hangar scheduled to become operational during 2026-27, which will significantly augment aerospace manufacturing capacity, alongside its existing 1,40,000 sq. ft. ADS manufacturing facility with dedicated Aerospace, Semiconductor and Defence capacity supporting execution of the cumulative order backlog over approximately five years. The Board approved the acquisition of 10 acres of land near Bengaluru International Airport as a strategic base for the next phase of ADS growth. A new manufacturing hub was established at Manesar through a long-term lease for passenger vehicle and two-wheeler components, while existing Pune and Pantnagar operations are being expanded, and the Sweden facility continues as a specialised hub for large-engine connecting rods serving marine and heavy-duty commercial vehicle applications. Machining capacity at existing facilities continues to expand, supported by a planned capex of Rs 2,500 mn over the next few years towards buildings, machinery and advanced manufacturing infrastructure. An in-house surface treatment facility is being commissioned to enable production of larger, more complex structural components and deepen vertical integration, and 5-axis machining capability has been extended from components of around 1.5 metres to components up to 4 metres. Future investments will focus on ADS capacity expansion, additional forging capacity at Pantnagar Plant 6, higher machining capacity at Bengaluru Plant 2, and the Nichidai-Sansera joint venture for technology-agnostic and xEV precision components, where a dedicated manufacturing facility is under development with equipment installation planned through 2026-27 and commercial production expected in the second half of 2026-27.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Revenue growth supported by core platform demand, new programme ramp-ups and strong momentum in ADS product sales.
- Margin improvement driven by operating leverage, productivity gains, automation, cost discipline, better utilisation and a richer business mix.
- PAT growth enabled by EBITDA expansion, lower finance cost and sharper execution across operating and financial levers.
- Business mix enhanced by rising contribution from non-automotive, technology-agnostic and xEV-linked opportunities.
- At home the automotive industry is experiencing a healthy recovery, with entry-level motorcycle and passenger vehicle segments poised for strong volume expansion in the year ahead, giving a stable domestic base.
- Aerospace order books remain at historic heights, reflecting sustained global demand, while the semiconductor industry is in a transformative upcycle driven by the worldwide race to build AI infrastructure.
- Stricter Regional Value Content requirements and a decisive shift towards localised manufacturing in North America are reshaping global supply chains and redrawing where value must be created.
- Demand is shifting towards larger, more complex and higher value-added components, aligning with Sansera's expanded machining capability.
- OEMs and global customers are prioritising dependable suppliers with manufacturing depth and quality systems, enhancing Sansera's relevance as a supply-chain-resilience and localisation beneficiary.
- Aerospace components require stringent quality standards, extended qualification cycles, traceability and material discipline, creating strong entry barriers that favour incumbent qualified suppliers.
- Semiconductor equipment components demand exacting dimensional accuracy, surface finish, cleanliness and material integrity, with long qualification cycles favouring trusted suppliers.
- Order inflows from international customers remained subdued during the year due to global macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty.
- India's automotive industry outlook is supported by improving consumer sentiment, better financing availability and resilient demand across two-wheelers, passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles and three-wheelers, sustaining demand for precision-engineered components.
- EV transition and hybrid adoption create opportunities in xEV and technology-agnostic products while supporting portfolio diversification.
- Key watch areas flagged by management: commodity prices, geopolitical uncertainty, logistics disruption, currency volatility and evolving policy frameworks, requiring continued cost discipline and supply-chain resilience.
- The secured order book stood at approximately Rs 19,194 million as of March 2026, representing the peak annual revenue potential of confirmed programmes including letters of intent and purchase orders where production has commenced after 1 April 2026 or is yet to begin.
- The order book is expected to reach peak annual revenue contribution over the next three years as programmes mature and production ramps up.
- The ADS business had a cumulative unexecuted order backlog of approximately Rs 44,638 million (Rs 44.6 bn) as of 31 March 2026, expected to be executed over the next five years, providing an unusual degree of multi-year revenue visibility.
- The order book as of 31 March 2026 includes programmes that entered mass production on or after 1 April 2026, whose full revenue potential is expected to be reflected progressively in the topline as they reach peak production levels.
- Order inflows from international customers remained subdued during the year due to prevailing global macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties, though the Company continues to actively pursue new orders across all business segments.
- The Value Creation Model cites a strong order book of Rs 19.2 bn as an input for the year.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Sansera operates 18 integrated manufacturing facilities, comprising 17 in India and one specialised facility in Sweden, and continued to expand its production network across both automotive and ADS businesses during FY2025-26. The Company commissioned the approximately 2.7 Lacs sq. ft. Pantnagar facility dedicated to crankshaft assemblies for the domestic two-wheeler segment, featuring IoT-enabled automation, and commenced regular production of semiconductor components. It is accelerating ADS expansion through a new 80,000 sq. ft. hangar scheduled to become operational during 2026-27, which will significantly augment aerospace manufacturing capacity, alongside its existing 1,40,000 sq. ft. ADS manufacturing facility with dedicated Aerospace, Semiconductor and Defence capacity supporting execution of the cumulative order backlog over approximately five years. The Board approved the acquisition of 10 acres of land near Bengaluru International Airport as a strategic base for the next phase of ADS growth. A new manufacturing hub was established at Manesar through a long-term lease for passenger vehicle and two-wheeler components, while existing Pune and Pantnagar operations are being expanded, and the Sweden facility continues as a specialised hub for large-engine connecting rods serving marine and heavy-duty commercial vehicle applications. Machining capacity at existing facilities continues to expand, supported by a planned capex of Rs 2,500 mn over the next few years towards buildings, machinery and advanced manufacturing infrastructure. An in-house surface treatment facility is being commissioned to enable production of larger, more complex structural components and deepen vertical integration, and 5-axis machining capability has been extended from components of around 1.5 metres to components up to 4 metres. Future investments will focus on ADS capacity expansion, additional forging capacity at Pantnagar Plant 6, higher machining capacity at Bengaluru Plant 2, and the Nichidai-Sansera joint venture for technology-agnostic and xEV precision components, where a dedicated manufacturing facility is under development with equipment installation planned through 2026-27 and commercial production expected in the second half of 2026-27.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Over four decades of precision engineering experience since incorporation in 1981, with customer relationships spanning generations of technology - 40% of client relationships are 20+ years old and a further 20% are 10+ years old.
- Scale-driven execution across 18 integrated manufacturing facilities (17 in India, one in Sweden) supported by more than 529 dedicated engineering specialists.
- In-house machine building and automation capability for customised robotic production lines and tooling, which enhances operational efficiency and optimises cost structures.
- Vertical integration through in-house surface treatment capability alongside forging and machining, enabling production of larger and more complex structural components.
- Advanced 5-axis machining capability extended from components of around 1.5 metres to components up to 4 metres, opening access to higher-complexity, higher-value contracts.
- Technology-agnostic portfolio spanning ICE, hybrid and xEV platforms, so the Company remains relevant across the mobility transition rather than exposed to a single powertrain.
- High entry barriers in aerospace and semiconductor equipment - stringent quality standards, extended qualification cycles, traceability and material discipline - which favour an already-qualified incumbent supplier.
- Diversified customer mix across industries, geographies and end-use applications, with associations spanning 23 leading domestic two-wheeler OEMs, 13 domestic EV OEMs, 16 global light vehicle OEMs and 12 global MHCV OEMs.
- Multi-year revenue visibility from a secured order book and a sizeable ADS unexecuted backlog executable over roughly five years.
- Serves 7+ sectors, providing diversification beyond a single end-market cycle.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization

Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
